nodes.name: long_press

nodes.summary: Taps at raw screen coordinates converted from the model's coordinate space.

nodes.name: click_area

nodes.name: type_text

nodes.name: system_button

nodes.name: swipe

nodes.name: open_bundle_id
nodes.summary: Opens an app by its exact package/bundle identifier, with a hint suggesting manual navigation on failure.

nodes.name: wait
nodes.summary: Pauses execution for a specified number of seconds.

nodes.name: remember
nodes.summary: Stores a piece of information in shared agent state for later recall.

nodes.name: complete
nodes.summary: Marks the current crawling task as complete with a success flag and final answer/reason.

nodes.name: type_secret
nodes.summary: Resolves a named credential via the credential manager and types it into an input field without exposing the secret value in logs.

nodes.name: AIInteractionItem
nodes.summary: List-item widget representing a single AI interaction entry in the monitor feed.

nodes.name: StepDetailWidget
nodes.summary: Expandable panel showing full detail (timings, request/response, prompt tree, raw response) for one crawl step.

nodes.name: AIMonitorPanel

nodes.summary: Parses a raw AI response payload to extract the structured list of parsed actions, handling both list and JSON-string encodings.

nodes.name: _extract_embedded_json
nodes.summary: Attempts to locate and parse a JSON object embedded within a raw AI response text, first trying a direct parse then falling back to a fenced-code-block regex extraction.

nodes.name: _build_timing_breakdown
nodes.summary: Aggregates a list of phase transitions into a per-phase timing breakdown used by the step detail view.

nodes.name: settings_panel.py
nodes.summary: Large tabbed settings panel covering general options, AI/crawler behavior, API keys, and third-party integrations (OmniParser, PCAPdroid, MobSF, tracing providers), with validation and persistence via the config manager.

nodes.name: SettingsPanel
nodes.summary: Tabbed settings UI exposing dozens of configuration getters/setters for crawl limits, API keys, integrations, and tracing, with input validation, keepalive pinging, and load/save/reset logic.

nodes.name: action_context.py
nodes.summary: Defines the ActionContext dataclass-like container that bundles the device driver, UI state, shared crawler state, state provider, credential manager, and workflow context passed into executor tool/action functions during a crawl session.

nodes.name: ActionContext
nodes.summary: Lightweight container class bundling the device driver, UI state, shared agent state, state provider, credential manager, and streaming/workflow context references passed into executor tools during a run, replacing the old `tools=tools_instance` parameter pattern.

nodes.name: crawler_agent.py
nodes.summary: Implements CrawlerAgent, the core LlamaIndex Workflow orchestrating device connection, tool registry setup, manager/executor/fast-agent loops, trajectory recording, and finalization for a mobile app crawl session.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the llama-index Workflow/@step pattern with async event handlers chaining StartEvent -> FastAgentExecuteEvent/ManagerInputEvent -> ExecutorInputEvent/ExecutorResultEvent -> FinalizeEvent -> StopEvent, and dynamically wires either a FastAgent-only path or a Manager+Executor reasoning path depending on config.

nodes.name: CrawlerAgent
nodes.summary: Main Workflow class that connects to an Android/iOS device, builds the tool registry (including MCP-discovered tools), runs the manager/executor/fast-agent step loop, records trajectories, and finalizes results with a structured summary and telemetry capture.

nodes.name: events.py
nodes.summary: Defines the dataclass event types (fast-agent, manager plan, executor, external user message, app-opener response, finalize, result) that route between the top-level CrawlerAgent workflow and its child agents during a crawl session.

nodes.name: FastAgentExecuteEvent
nodes.summary: Event carrying the instruction dispatched to the fast agent for a single subgoal execution.

nodes.name: FastAgentResultEvent
nodes.summary: Event reporting the fast agent's execution outcome, including success flag, reason, and the originating instruction.

nodes.name: ManagerInputEvent
nodes.summary: Event marking the input handed to the manager/planning agent to begin a planning step.

nodes.name: ManagerPlanEvent
nodes.summary: Event carrying the manager's updated plan, current subgoal, reasoning thought, and completion status (success/answer), used for workflow step routing between ManagerAgent and CrawlerAgent.

nodes.name: ExecutorInputEvent
nodes.summary: Event carrying the current subgoal handed to the executor agent for atomic action execution.

nodes.name: ExecutorResultEvent
nodes.summary: Event reporting the executor's action outcome, any error encountered, and a human-readable summary.

nodes.name: ExternalUserMessageAppliedEvent
nodes.summary: Event recording that one or more external user messages were applied at a given step, noting the consumer and step number.

nodes.name: ExternalUserMessageDroppedEvent
nodes.summary: Event recording that one or more external user messages were dropped at a given step, along with the reason.

nodes.name: AppOpenerResponseEvent
nodes.summary: Event carrying an LLM result produced by the AppOpener workflow (success flag, package name, prompt, response, and summary) so it can be surfaced in the AI Monitor.

nodes.name: FinalizeEvent
nodes.summary: Event signaling that the crawl session should finalize, carrying a success flag and a reason.

nodes.name: ResultEvent
nodes.summary: Terminal event carrying the crawl's overall success flag, reason, step history, and any structured output produced; returned by CrawlerAgent.run().

nodes.name: crawler_agent_service.py
nodes.summary: Central orchestration service that configures, runs, instruments, and tears down the AI crawler agent, wiring together config resolution, device/app readiness checks, OmniParser/OTel instrumentation, step-phase tracking, AI-interaction/AI-Monitor logging, and result conversion.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large (2012-line) service class combining logging setup, LLM config/API-key resolution, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, step-phase state machine wiring, screenshot/AI-interaction persistence for the AI Monitor, and workflow cancellation handling in one component.

nodes.name: CancelledErrorFilter
nodes.summary: Logging filter that suppresses noisy asyncio.CancelledError stack traces from ERROR-level logs during task cancellation.

nodes.name: CrawlerLogHandler
nodes.summary: Custom logging handler that writes structured JSON log records to a per-run log file for later diagnostics.

nodes.name: CrawlerGoal
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing the exploration goal given to the agent, including description, max steps, reasoning mode, and target app package.

nodes.name: CrawlerRunResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass summarizing the outcome of a crawler run: success flag, steps completed, actions taken, final state, error message, and duration.

nodes.name: CrawlerAgentService
nodes.summary: Top-level agent orchestrator: resolves LLM/config settings, ensures the device and target app are ready, initializes OmniParser and OpenTelemetry instrumentation, tracks step-phase transitions, wires action verification/UI-wait/context-recovery observers, persists AI-interaction and screenshot data for the AI Monitor, executes the exploration task, and logs/cleans up afterward.

nodes.name: AI_MONITOR_PLAN.md

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Mobile Crawler is a PySide6 desktop tool that drives an AI agent to autonomously explore Android apps over ADB, capturing screenshots, UI state, and telemetry along the way. The README explains the project's purpose, its vision-based grounding via OmniParser, traffic capture with MobSF, and how the CLI and GUI both drive the same underlying crawl engine. Use this as the map for the rest of the tour: from here we descend into the GUI, the CLI, the core orchestration layer, the embedded AI agent runtime, and finally the persistence and reporting subsystems it all feeds into.

tour.title: GUI Entry Point
tour.description: main_window.py is the PySide6 desktop entry point, exposed as the mobile-crawler-gui console script and started via its module-level run() function. With a fan-out of 33 edges it is the single most far-reaching file in the codebase: it wires together the device/app/AI selectors, settings panel, crawl controller, statistics dashboard, and every other UI panel into one cohesive crawl-and-monitor experience. Because nothing else imports it (fan-in of 0), it sits at the very top of the dependency graph -- the natural starting point for tracing how a click in the UI eventually reaches an Android device.
tour.languageLesson: PySide6 (Qt for Python) apps are built around signals and slots: widgets emit signals on user interaction, and slots (ordinary methods) subscribe to react to them, decoupling UI events from business logic.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: Alongside the GUI, Mobile Crawler ships a Click-based command-line interface. cli/main.py defines the top-level command group and wires together the crawl, config, report, list, and delete subcommands, while cli/commands/crawl.py is the workhorse that assembles configuration, opens the database, and launches a full crawl run, emitting JSON events to stdout for scripting. Both doors -- GUI and CLI -- lead into the same core orchestration layer covered next, showing a clean separation between interface and engine.

tour.title: Core Orchestration Layer
tour.description: Whichever entry point launches a crawl, control flows into the Core Orchestration layer. crawler_loop.py runs the crawl on a background thread and delegates traversal to the crawler agent service; crawl_state_machine.py enforces valid lifecycle transitions (idle to running to paused to stopped) and notifies listeners; crawl_controller.py exposes thread-safe pause/resume/stop semantics that the UI and CLI both call into. This layer keeps a long-running, potentially flaky Android exploration session controllable and observable.
tour.languageLesson: The state machine pattern encodes valid transitions explicitly rather than scattering if/else checks throughout the code, making illegal states (like resuming a crawl that never started) unrepresentable.

tour.title: Configuration Management
tour.description: Before a crawl can run, its behavior is shaped by the Configuration layer. config_manager.py is the central accessor that layers persisted user settings on top of environment-variable overrides with automatic type coercion; defaults.py seeds sane defaults when nothing else is configured; paths.py resolves the OS-specific application data directory used for the database, logs, and session artifacts. Every subsystem from here on -- the agent, the database, the report generator -- reads its settings through this layer rather than hardcoding values.

tour.title: Bridging to the AI Agent
tour.description: crawler_agent_service.py is the central orchestration service that configures, runs, instruments, and tears down the AI crawler agent -- with a fan-out of 22 it is the second most far-reaching file in the project. It resolves configuration from Step 5, wires up device connections, telemetry, and traffic/video capture, then hands control to the embedded agent runtime explored next. Think of it as the adapter between Mobile Crawler's own orchestration layer and the internalized AI agent sub-application.

tour.title: The Crawler Agent Runtime
tour.description: domain/crawler_agent is an internalized AI agent sub-application (formerly a DroidRun fork) that actually drives on-device exploration. Its core, agent/droid/crawler_agent.py, is a LlamaIndex Workflow with the highest fan-out in the codebase (32 edges): it orchestrates device connection, tool registry setup, and the manager/executor/fast-agent decision loop step by step. This is where the 'AI' in AI-Powered Android Exploration actually lives -- everything before this step was plumbing to get here.
tour.languageLesson: LlamaIndex Workflows model an agent as a graph of @step-decorated methods that consume and emit typed Event objects, turning what would otherwise be a tangled state machine into an explicit, testable pipeline.

tour.title: Manager and Fast-Agent Strategies
tour.description: The CrawlerAgent from Step 7 can delegate its decision-making to different strategies. manager_agent.py maintains full conversation history and enriches its prompts with app-card context for careful, stateful reasoning; stateless_manager_agent.py trades that context continuity for a bounded action history to cut token usage; fast_agent.py takes a different approach entirely, generating and streaming XML-formatted tool calls in a code-generation style loop. Swapping between these lets the project trade cost, speed, and reasoning depth per app or per step.
tour.languageLesson: This is the Strategy pattern: multiple interchangeable agent implementations share a common workflow contract, so the CrawlerAgent can select one at runtime without changing its own code.

tour.title: Device Driver Abstraction
tour.description: Whatever strategy is choosing actions, those actions ultimately need to reach a real device. driver/base.py defines the DeviceDriver interface -- tap, swipe, text entry, screenshots, app control -- that every platform-specific implementation must satisfy, plus a DeviceDisconnectedError for connectivity loss. driver/android.py is the concrete ADB-based implementation, providing raw Android I/O with automatic reconnect handling. This abstraction is what would let the project add an iOS driver without touching the agent logic above it.
tour.languageLesson: Defining an abstract interface for DeviceDriver lets the rest of the codebase depend on a stable contract rather than a concrete Android implementation -- a classic dependency-inversion technique in Python.

tour.title: Vision-Based Grounding
tour.description: To decide where to tap, the agent needs to understand what's on screen -- that's grounding. providers/registry.py fetches and caches available AI model lists from Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama, detecting which support vision input; vision_detector.py provides a unified interface to validate vision-capable models across those providers; grounding/dtos.py defines the immutable OCR detection and overlay data structures the OmniParser/SoM pipeline produces. Together these let the agent ground its instructions, such as 'tap the login button', in actual pixel coordinates.

tour.title: Persistence Layer
tour.description: Every crawl run's data lands in SQLite. infrastructure/database.py owns the persistent connection, applies pragmas, and defines/migrates the schema; run_repository.py provides CRUD and query operations over the `runs` table via a typed Run dataclass. The underlying schema is defined in migrations/001_initial_schema.sql: the `runs` table tracks each crawl session's metadata, while `screens` stores every unique screen discovered, keyed by composite and visual hashes -- database.py alone has the highest fan-in in the whole codebase (14 dependents), reflecting how central persistence is to every other subsystem.
tour.languageLesson: SQL schema migrations are applied incrementally and should be idempotent -- 011_add_session_path.sql, for instance, only adds one column to the existing `runs` table rather than redefining it.

tour.title: Traffic and Video Capture
tour.description: Alongside UI exploration, the crawler captures forensic evidence of what the app actually does. traffic_capture_manager.py manages the full lifecycle of PCAPdroid-based network traffic capture, including handling on-device consent dialogs; video_recording_manager.py records rotating screen-recording segments via ADB screenrecord and stitches them into a manifest; mobsf_manager.py integrates with a local MobSF instance to extract, scan, and retrieve a static security report for the APK. These three run alongside the agent loop from Steps 7-10, and their output feeds directly into the reporting stage next.

tour.title: Report Generation
tour.description: Once a crawl finishes, the Reporting layer turns raw data into a readable artifact. correlator.py stitches together run/step data with parsed PCAP traffic (via pcap_parser.py's dpkt-based HTTP/HTTPS extraction) and MobSF security findings (via mobsf_parser.py) into a unified RunReportData timeline; generator.py then renders that timeline through Jinja2 templates into a self-contained HTML report. This closes the loop from Step 12's raw capture data to a human-readable deliverable.
tour.languageLesson: Jinja2 templates separate presentation from logic: generator.py builds a plain Python data structure (RunReportData) and hands it to a template, keeping HTML markup out of the report-building code.

tour.title: Architecture Reference
tour.description: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is the canonical architecture reference, describing the same layered system this tour just walked through end-to-end: interface (Steps 2-3), core orchestration (Step 4), domain services and the crawler agent runtime (Steps 6-10), and infrastructure and reporting (Steps 11-13). Reading it now, after seeing the actual code, should make each layer's boundary and responsibility concrete rather than abstract -- use it going forward as the map back to any subsystem you need to revisit.
